key_insight: An LLM agent uses physics-based simulations to inverse-design fabrication recipes for desired depth profiles of implanted ions or vacancies.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help translate spatial material designs into ion-processing recipes for graded materials, metamaterials, and quantum superlattices.
method: Specify a target ion or vacancy depth profile.
Select ion species, energies, incident angles, and target material layers.
Write, run, and interpret ion–matter simulations, iteratively refining the recipe.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulated profile matching with minimal human input, but provides no quantitative accuracy metrics or experimental fabrication validation.
watch_item: Practical deployment requires validating that simulator-designed recipes reproduce target profiles in fabricated materials.
paper_title: Agentic inverse design of spatially programmed materials
